slides.title: Welcome to the Children's Constitution Club!
slides.tip: Play welcome music. Confirm everyone is seated in groups.

slides.title: Setting Up the Change Champion Zone
body: Now that you have prepared the box, please hand it over to me.
I will place it in a corner at the front of the classroom.
It is everyone's responsibility to make sure this box is not lost or moved elsewhere.
Each Core Committee member should take on the responsibility of reminding the teacher to read the change stories from the box.
Let us all encourage each other to bring about change!
slides.tip: Collect the box and place it at the front of the class.

slides.title: Change Stories
body: Hey CMCA Champions! Do you have any change stories to share? Maybe you helped someone, solved a problem, showed kindness, or took a small step to make a situation better.
If you have such a story, write it on a slip of paper and put it in the Change Champion Box!
If you don't have a story yet, that's okay! You can bring about a change anytime, notice the difference it makes, and then share your story with us later.
Remember, every big change begins with a small action!
So come forward, create small ripples of change, and don't forget to tell us about them!
slides.tip: If students have stories ready, ask them to put them in the CC Box.

slides.title: Ajay's Story
body: While Ajay was playing cricket with some friends, he suddenly heard a painful sound. He traced it to a nearby pit. A puppy was stuck there and could not get out. The pit was too deep for him to pull the puppy out.

The boy quickly ran home and asked his father to call the animal rescue helpline. While waiting for help, he stayed near the pit trying to calm the puppy. After 20 minutes, the animal rescue team arrived and safely brought the puppy out.
slides.tip: Ask a student volunteer to read the story on screen aloud.

slides.title: Reflecting on Ajay's Story
body: How did this story make you feel? Did it make you happy, sad, surprised, or thoughtful?
Animals may not be able to speak like us, but they too have rights! Can anyone tell some of those rights?
They are: the right to food, the right to medical care, the right to compassion, and the right to shelter.
slides.tip: Pause 10 seconds for responses after each question.

slides.title: Reflecting on Ajay's Story
body: Can you share an instance when you have helped animals?
It could be something as simple as feeding a dog, keeping water out for birds, helping an injured or sick animal, or supporting an animal shelter with your family.

slides.title: Child Rights & Responsibilities
body: Today let us understand the 'rights' that are reserved especially for you as children.
Of course, with every right comes...? Yes, you said it right — responsibilities!
So today we will look at both child rights and responsibilities.

slides.title: Introduction to Child Rights
body: Are you all seated in your groups? Now, I have a fun challenge for your groups!
We are going to guess some rights and responsibilities by looking at picture clues.
It will be like a picture quiz! But there's a special twist here...
The rights we will explore today are not just ordinary rights. They are special rights guaranteed to all children.
Do you know what they are called?
That's right! They are called Child Rights!
slides.tip: Pause 3 seconds for the answer 'Child Rights'.

slides.title: Group Work — Guess Rights from Pictures
slides.brief: Look at all the pictures in the handout, discuss in your groups, and list child rights and responsibilities. Write as clearly as possible.
slides.tip: Distribute handouts to each group. 5 minute timer.

slides.title: Group Work — Swap Sheets
slides.brief: Exchange your sheet with the group next to you. Look at the pictures in the other group's sheet and try to add any child rights or responsibilities they may have missed.
slides.tip: Draw 4 boxes on the board labelled SURVIVAL, PARTICIPATION, DEVELOPMENT, and PROTECTION. Keep flash cards ready.

slides.title: Child Rights & the UN Convention
body: We are now going to share the work we did in our groups. But before that, can anyone tell what you understand by the term 'Child Rights'?
Every child from birth until they turn 18 is guaranteed child rights. These rights protect children and help them receive nutritious food, good healthcare, rest, and education.
Look at the board! These rights can be divided into four major categories:
Survival, Protection, Development, and Participation.
What do you understand by Survival Rights, and why are they important?
What do you understand by Protection Rights, and why are they important?
What do you understand by Development Rights, and why are they important?
What do you understand by Participation Rights, and why are they important?
slides.tip: Write the rights under each category on the board. Ask students to hold up the flash cards.

slides.title: Group Sharing
body: One member from each group will now take turns sharing only the child rights (not responsibilities) from your sheets.
Let us try to avoid repeating what others have already said.
slides.tip: Ask students to hold the relevant flash card as each right is read.

slides.title: ChildLine
body: If you or a child you know ever needs help, including issues like child labour or child marriage, you can call 1098 (ChildLine) or talk to an adult you trust for support.
slides.tip: Write 1098 ChildLine number on the board.

slides.title: Reflection
body: Take a sheet of paper. Answer a few simple questions honestly.
questions: Which child right do you like the most?
Do you feel you receive this right in your life?
Do you feel all children receive this right?
What is one thing you can do to support this right for yourself or others?
slides.tip: Display questions one by one. Click 'next' after all answers.

slides.title: Introduction to Makkala Grama Sabha
body: Have you ever participated in any meeting where adults really listen to children?
Did you know there is a special meeting just for children? It is called the Makkala Grama Sabha.
Here children talk about issues related to them like school, safety, and play!
If you got a chance to speak at that meeting, what would you like to tell your village leaders?
slides.tip: Show MGS images. Pause for children's responses.

slides.title: Wrap-up
slides.tip: Play MC video. Encourage students to put stories in the CC box.
kn_script: Hey Change Champions! Did you know that every big change begins with a small step?
Maybe you helped someone, solved a problem, showed kindness, or made your community a little better. No action is too small when it comes to bringing about change!
So don't forget to share your 'Ripple of Change' story. Write it on your sheet — tell us what you did and how it made a difference.
After writing, carefully fold your sheet... and put it in the Change Champion Box!
Who knows? The small ripple you create today could become a big wave of change tomorrow!
Are you ready, Champions? Let's fill the box with amazing stories! Thank you.
